title: Pagasa 7 mungbean (UPL Mg 7): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Pagasa 7 mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Pagasa 7 mungbean is a mungbean variety. About 66 days to harvest, 1.7 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Pagasa 7 is a registered mungbean variety, also sold or known as UPL Mg 7 or munggo Pag asa 7. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1989. IPB bred it. It takes about 66 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for UPL Mg 7 or munggo Pag asa 7, this is the same mungbean. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [mungbean variety finder](/crop-varieties/mungbean), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

items: **Days to harvest:** about 66 days from sowing to harvest.
**Yield:** 1.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Pagasa 7 mungbean takes about 66 days from sowing to harvest. That is 6.2 days longer than the average of the 33 mungbean varieties with a day count, 59.8 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.68 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.25. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 66 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It was weak against powdery mildew, so scout for it from the early weeks. Read up on [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot).

The pests and diseases that hit mungbean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: Registered in 1989 with the Philippine Seed Board.
Drought tolerant, does well in partial shade.
Susceptible to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to Cercospora leaf spot.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the long time standard munggo: used as the farmer check in Ilocos Norte on farm trials of the 1990s, part of IPB's Pag asa series. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Pagasa 7 mungbean

Munggo is ready in about two months, so it fits the gap after rice. Pick a variety that ripens its pods together, which saves picking rounds, and one rated against cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is UPL Mg 7 the same as Pagasa 7?
items.a: Yes. UPL Mg 7 is another name for Pagasa 7. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 66 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.68 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Pagasa 7?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
